text:
Predicates:
RegisterToVoteInUS(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
ParticipateInElection2024(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
USCitizen(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
TaiwaneseCitizen(x) ::: x holds Taiwanese citizenship.
RussianFederationOfficial(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
ManagerAtGazprom(x) ::: x is a manager at Gazprom.
Premises:
∀x (RegisterToVoteInUS(x) → ParticipateInElection2024(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
∀x (USCitizen(x) → RegisterToVoteInUS(x)) ::: If someone has United States citizenship, then they can register to vote in the United States.
∀x (USCitizen(x) ⊕ TaiwaneseCitizen(x)) ::: A person either has United States citizenship or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬∃x (RussianFederationOfficial(x) ∧ TaiwaneseCitizen(x)) ::: No Russian Federation officials hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬(TaiwaneseCitizen(vladimir) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(vladimir)) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
RegisterToVoteInUS(ekaterina) ⊕ RussianFederationOfficial(ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote in the United States, or she is a Russian Federation official.
Conclusion:
RussianFederationOfficial(vladimir) ::: Vladimir is a Russian Federation official.
